mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a 20-day S&P 500 forward return positive as investors anticipate rate hikes later in the cycle.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in a given month
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day pre-inflation cross point (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeding 144,000 in a month predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return via increased consumer confidence and corporate hiring.
failure_condition: Across 12 consecutive months with PAYEMS > 144,000, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly above the 60-day mean when PAYEMS <= 144,000 (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in the monthly GDPC1 personal consumption expenditure by at least 2% signals weakening near-term demand, producing a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by ≥2% in a month
failure_condition: In 5 consecutive months with GDPC1 declines ≥2%, the 20-day forward return mean is not lower than the 20-day mean during prior stable demand months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO manufacturing index below 98.0 coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing output forecasts tighter supply chains and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: Over 4 consecutive INDPRO < 98.0 months, 20-day forward returns are not statistically worse than during INDPRO ≥ 98.0 months (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.2% in a month, the 60-day S&P 500 forward return is expected to turn negative as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs eroding equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.2% in a month
failure_condition: Across 10 consecutive months with FEDFUNDS up >0.2%, the 60-day forward return mean is not lower than the 60-day mean during prior months with FEDFUNDS increases ≤0.2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained two-month decline in UNRATE below 5.5% increases the probability of a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as lower unemployment is interpreted as a pro-equity regime.
failure_condition: In 5 consecutive months with UNRATE < 5.5%, the 20-day forward return mean is not higher than the 20-day mean during prior months with UNRATE ≥ 5.5% (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both HOUST and RSAFS below 1400 and 600 million dollars, respectively, indicate softening demand in both retail and credit sectors, leading to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 1400 AND RSAFS < 600 in the same month
failure_condition: During 10 consecutive months with both proxies below thresholds, the 20-day forward return mean is not lower than during months where at least one proxy is at or above its threshold (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to post-crisis supply resilience (indicated by INDPRO > 105 and RSAFS > 620 million for two consecutive months) is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates sustained production capacity.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 105 AND RSAFS > 620 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 12 months with both proxies in the resilient zone, the 60-day forward return mean is not higher than the 60-day mean during prior months in the weak-supply regime (bootstrap p > 0.05).
